-73.98550,40.75450.name: Spring Fertility-New York
-73.98550,40.75450.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Catha Fischer, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

135.19438,34.69324.name: Kobe Innovative Center
135.19438,34.69324.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of SENJU Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.33269,51.56497.name: London Women's Clinic Harrow
-0.33269,51.56497.state: The Clementine Churchill, Harrow, Sudbury Hill, HA1 3RX
-0.33269,51.56497.company: Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic
-0.33269,51.56497.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to London Women's Clinic. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

126.91200,37.57200.name: Sooam Biotech
126.91200,37.57200.desc: The South Korean laboratory that commercialised pet cloning, founded by a researcher whose stem-cell papers were retracted for fabrication and who was convicted of embezzlement. He returned to a business with no regulatory gatekeeper at all: cloning a dog requires no biosafety approval anywhere, because nothing foreign is inserted. A career ended by scientific fraud continued in the part of the field that asks no questions. Producing the first cloned dog in 2005 reportedly took 1,000 embryos implanted into 123 surrogate mothers.

4.38100,50.84200.name: CropLife International
4.38100,50.84200.desc: The trade association of the four majors and their peers, coordinating industry positions on pesticide and biotechnology regulation worldwide. Its member fees exceed what most members declare in lobbying spend in their own names. An association can hold a position no individual company wants recorded against it.

-77.04100,38.84800.name: USDA APHIS — biotechnology compliance complaints
-77.04100,38.84800.desc: Takes reports that a permit holder has broken the conditions of a release: planting outside the authorised area, failing to maintain isolation distances, leaving volunteers standing after harvest. It has an inspection service and it publishes enforcement actions, so a report can end in a penalty. What it will not do is reconsider whether the release should have been approved — for that the window was the comment period. Quote the permit number; without it a report is hard to route and easy to lose.

-78.24640,37.50790.name: Envigo — Cumberland County breeding facility
-78.24640,37.50790.desc: A dog-breeding facility supplying research beagles was shut in October 2022 after documented welfare violations. Around four thousand animals were removed, 446 of them in acute distress, and 3,776 were placed for adoption. The conditions recorded included dogs killed by injection to the heart without proper anaesthetic, and survivors with rotting teeth. It belongs on this map for two reasons beyond the animals. First, it is the largest single removal of research animals from a US supplier, and it happened under welfare inspection rather than through any biosafety route. Second, the executives involved reappear: the chief operating officer at the time of those violations later became chief executive of a company proposing a new macaque breeding facility, which is how a community in Georgia came to learn the history of the people asking to build next door.
